pride_data.title: Mapping the interactome of OSCC prognostic-associated proteins NDRG1 and PGK1 through proximity labeling using TurboID
pride_data.projectDescription: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a prevalent type of head and neck cancer, accounting for more than 90% of all oral malignancies worldwide. The identification of diagnostic and prognostic markers for OSCC is crucial for improving patient outcomes, as early detection and treatment are critical for successful management of this disease. In this regard, our group recently demonstrated that N-myc downstream-regulated gene 1 (NDRG1) and phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (PGK1) are prognostic markers in OSCC, however, little is known about the role of these proteins in OSCC development. To better understand their signaling pathways, we used TurboID-based proximity labeling to identify the interactomes of NDRG1 and PGK1 in HEK293 cells. Here, protein abundance patterns associated with three distinct time-points were utilized for protein clustering, allowing the identification of protein clusters with a “fast” or “slow” response to biotin. Functional enrichment of GO terms revealed processes mostly associated with mRNA processing for both PGK1 and NDRG1 “fast” clusters, while GO processes related to protein localization and catalytic activity were identified in PGK1 and NDRG1 “slow” clusters, respectively. A total of 65 out of 361 proteins from different clusters were also identified in neoplastic islands of OSCC tissues from our previous study. Additionally, 28 of these proteins have their gene expression associated with prognostic features such as death, metastasis and/or relapse in OSCC patients. Ultimately, our data enabled the identification of 17 previously known physical interactions and functional associations among these proteins, as well as 30 new putative interactions, characterizing a prognostic-associated interactome composed of 28 proteins. This interactome enables the prioritization of candidates that can be further explored in OSCC progression.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: HEK293 cells were transfected for 48 hours with TurboID (herein called “Empty Vector”), TurboID-NDRG1 or TurboID-PGK1 and grown in three 150 mm² plates for each transfection, totalizing nine 150 mm² plates. After transfection, one plate of each construct was immediately harvested (0 h control) and the other two were incubated with 50 µM biotin for 1 h or 6 h. After reaching desired incubation times, cells were harvested with trypsin/EDTA, washed with PBS, incubated with 1 mL of lysis buffer containing 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 8M Urea, 1 mM DTT, 1 mM PMSF, 1% Triton X-100 and protease inhibitor cocktail (Roche) and sonicated on ice at 20% amplitude (Sonics Vibra-Cell VCX 500 sonicator). After lysate clarification, proteins were quantified using Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit and 300 µg of lysate were incubated with 100 µL of pre-equilibrated Streptavidin Sepharose beads (Cytiva) overnight at 4 °C. After washing steps, 10% of sample volume was aliquoted for western blotting, while the remaining 90% were submitted to on-beads digestion for LC-MS/MS analysis. For that, streptavidin beads were resuspended in 200 μL of 8M Urea, reduced with 5 mM DTT for 25 minutes at 56 °C, alkylated with 14 mM iodoacetamide for 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark, followed by urea dilution to a final concentration of 1.6 M using 50 mM NH4HCO3. For protein digestion, 1 mM of CaCl2 and 1 μg of trypsin were added and samples were incubated overnight at 37 °C in a Thermomixer. On the following day, the reaction was quenched adding a final volume of 0.4% TFA and samples were desalted with C18 StageTips. After desalting, samples were dried on a vacuum concentrator, resuspended in 0.1% formic acid, and stored at -20 °C until LC-MS/MS analysis.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data was processed using MaxQuant v2.0.1.0 and protein identification was performed against the UniProt Human Protein Database (containing 97,511 protein sequences, released in February 2021) using the Andromeda search engine. Carbamidomethylation of cysteines (+57.02 Da) was set as fixed modifications, and protein N-terminal acetylation (+42.01 Da) and methionine oxidation (+15.99 Da) were set as variable modifications. Trypsin/P was set as the proteolytic enzyme, with a maximum of two missed cleavages allowed. A tolerance of 10 ppm for precursor ions and 1 Da for fragment ions was defined. The FDR was estimated by the target-decoy method and set to a maximum of 1% at both protein and peptide levels. Label-free protein quantification was carried out by the MaxLFQ algorithm, using a minimal ratio count of one and a 2-minute window for matching between runs. Two searches were performed, one including Empty Vector and TurboID-PGK1 data and another containing Empty Vector and TurboID-NDRG1 data and their respective time point raw files. Results were exported from MaxQuant and further analyzed in Perseus v2.0.9.025, where contaminants, reverse sequences, and identifications “only by site” were excluded. LFQ intensity values were log2-transformed and missing values were imputed from a normal distribution, with an imputation width of 0.3 and a down-shift of 1.8. Average log2 LFQ values of technical replicates were calculated and utilized in further analysis.
